NNS Dependence

Source: R/Dependence.R
NNS.dep.Rd

Returns the dependence and nonlinear correlation between two variables based on higher order partial moment matrices measured by frequency or area.

Usage

NNS.dep(x, y = NULL, asym = FALSE, p.value = FALSE, print.map = FALSE)

Arguments

x

a numeric vector, matrix or data frame.

y

NULL (default) or a numeric vector with compatible dimensions to x.

asym

logical; FALSE (default) returns the symmetric measures. If TRUE, returns the asymmetric (directional) measures: the partition is built on x only and the result measures the dependence of y on x (y as a function of x); swap the arguments for the other direction.

p.value

logical; FALSE (default) If TRUE (bivariate only), compares the results against 100 random permutations of y: the Dependence p-value is the upper-tail permutation p-value (1 + #(null >= observed)) / (1 + 100), the Correlation p-value is the two-sided permutation p-value min(1, 2 * min(1 + #(null <= observed), 1 + #(null >= observed)) / (1 + 100)), and the 95 percent intervals of the permutation null are returned (and plotted when print.map = TRUE).

print.map

logical; FALSE (default) Plots quadrant means, or p-value replicates.

Value

Returns the bi-variate "Correlation" and "Dependence" or correlation / dependence matrix for matrix input.

Details

Dependence is read from the recursive mean-split partitions of the data (NNS.part): on x (y as a function of x), on y, and on the joint quadrants of (x, y), where the co-lower, co-upper and divergent partial moments live. In every cell the degree-0 (frequency) and degree-1 (area) concordance about the cell means is measured against its expectation under the within-cell permutation null and rescaled so that perfect dependence stays at 1, and the two are averaged. The cell-size weighted average is taken at every level of each partition, from the whole sample down to the finest cells, and Dependence is the strongest level, so dependence carried between coarse cells (a noisy linear relationship), within fine cells (a nonlinear function) or by the joint quadrants (a circle, or y = x * noise) is detected alike. With asym = TRUE only the partition on x is used. A cell in which x is constant scores whether y is determined there (1 if y is constant, 0 otherwise), against the chance of that under the permutation null; in the joint quadrants such a cell is constant by construction and scores 0. Independent variables score near 0. Taking the strongest level adds a small selection effect, about 0.14 at n = 100 and 0.04 at n = 1000 for independent continuous data. It is larger for a rare discrete y, because each cell constant in x then contributes a single, weakly informative observation of whether y is determined there (about 0.12 at n = 300 and 0.05 at n = 1000 for a 3 percent binary y against a 20-level x). That score, like every cell term, is measured against its exact null and stays unbiased, so perfect dependence still reads 1; the p.value permutation null includes the selection effect. Levels below chance can make every average negative; Dependence is floored at 0, and Correlation, the signed average at the same level, never exceeds it in absolute value.

Note

For asymmetrical (asym = TRUE) matrices, entry [i, j] is the directional dependence ([row variable i] —> [column variable j]), i.e. NNS.dep(x[, i], x[, j], asym = TRUE), the dependence of column j on row variable i.

References

Viole, F. and Nawrocki, D. (2013) "Nonlinear Nonparametric Statistics: Using Partial Moments" (ISBN: 1490523995, 2nd edition: https://ovvo-financial.github.io/NNS/book/)

Author

Fred Viole, OVVO Financial Systems

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
set.seed(123)
x <- rnorm(100) ; y <- rnorm(100)
NNS.dep(x, y)

## Correlation / Dependence Matrix
x <- rnorm(100) ; y <- rnorm(100) ; z <- rnorm(100)
B <- cbind(x, y, z)
NNS.dep(B)
} # }
